stated_limitation: In the lower-yield sessions the effect does not reach significance against this conservative null, so the continuity result rests on the best-recorded session, while the correlation preservation is robust across all five.

justification.dataset: Dandiset 000056 (Peyrache ADn head-direction recordings) is the canonical dataset for the HD ring-attractor phenomenon, five sessions across five mice.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile, HD angle correctly derived from dual-LED difference with sentinel handling, states table used, units sorted and quality-filtered by MVL plus a null.
justification.analysis: Circular statistics throughout, with three appropriate and distinct null distributions (random-time for HD cells, label-permutation for correlation preservation, rate-preserving circular time-shift for bump continuity).
justification.correctness: Every headline number reproduces from the committed run logs, is internally consistent with the figures, physically possible, and rests on adequate samples and correct tests.
justification.figures: Figures are labeled with units and sample sizes, show tuning curves tiling the circle, a tracking bump, and the sleep correlation structure clearly; the example REM window is honestly labeled as a display window while claims rest on full-episode statistics.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate and the write-up explicitly names its weaknesses, that bump continuity holds only in the largest-ensemble session and one NREM test is non-significant in the smallest ensemble.
justification.verdict: Sound, replicated, honestly caveated reproduction of the Peyrache 2015 result; I would accept it.
